pool-1.query: pool wait p99 jumped and active connections are pinned at the pool max while concurrent requests are well above it; database query time stays flat and no requests fail yet

pool-2.query: a config change lowered POOL_MAX_SIZE just before the alarm; requests queue for a connection and pool wait becomes most of request latency

pool-3.query: requests on every route fail with TimeoutError acquiring connection from pool after waiting the full acquire timeout; the error rate climbs each minute

pool-4.query: latency alarm: p99 over the threshold, and the time is spent waiting for a pool slot, not in the database; payments-api latency is normal

pool-5.query: the error rate started rising minutes after pool wait began climbing; the failing lines show pool_wait_time_ms at the acquire timeout and a smaller pool_max_size than before

pool-6.query: connections pinned at a small pool size while concurrency rises; the database itself is not slow, so requests are waiting for a connection, not for their queries

pool-7.query: 500s on all routes from a pool-acquisition timeout raised in the database connection code; the failing version has been live for days, so no code deploy is involved

deploy-1.query: the error rate jumped from zero within seconds of a new deploy; every failing line is the same TypeError with a stack trace, served by the new version

deploy-2.query: 500s on POST /checkout only, all served by the newly deployed version; latency, pool wait and payments-api stay normal

deploy-3.query: the failures are specific to checkouts with has_promo false; requests that carry a promo still succeed on the new release

deploy-4.query: a release went out seconds before the errors began; failing requests return 500 in milliseconds, before any database or payments call

deploy-5.query: the same exception in a pricing function on every failing request, all on the new version and none on the old one

deploy-6.query: a steady share of checkouts fails with an unhandled exception since the deploy; the error alarm fired while the latency and pool-wait alarms stayed OK

deploy-7.query: the only change right before the new errors is a deploy; the earlier config changes are hours old and touch other code paths, so they are not the cause

downstream-1.query: payments-api p99 jumped in the same minute checkout p99 rose; checkout's own pool wait and DB query time stay flat

downstream-2.query: POST /checkout requests spend most of their latency waiting on payments-api, and some hit the upstream timeout and return 504 UpstreamTimeout

downstream-3.query: latency only on POST /checkout while /products and /cart/items stay normal; payments timeouts appear for the first time

downstream-4.query: the dependency became slow, not this service: upstream_latency_ms accounts for most of latency_ms in the slow requests, and no deploy or config change fits the onset

downstream-5.query: latency alarm with no failed requests at first; payments_p99_ms climbs toward the upstream timeout

downstream-6.query: checkout calls to the payments service slowed sharply; the connection pool never queues, so pool exhaustion is ruled out

slowdb-1.query: db_query_p50_ms rose on every route along with pool wait; connections stay busy longer and payments-api is normal

slowdb-2.query: queries are slow once a connection is acquired: query time climbed across all routes, not just checkout, and latency followed it

surge-1.query: the request rate rose sharply, with concurrent_max and pool_active_max rising in proportion; err% stays at zero and p50 is unchanged

surge-2.query: req climbed and then levelled off while callers say requests fail, with nothing in this service's logs; concurrent_max stays well under the concurrency cap and latency is normal

throttle-1.query: concurrent_max is flat at the function's concurrency cap; req stopped rising while callers keep sending, and the requests that do run are slow

throttle-2.query: callers get errors this service never logs, err% stays low, and concurrency is pinned at the reserved limit

leak-1.query: a steady stream of cold starts at steady traffic; requests vanish without log lines, err% stays low, and pool and payments-api are flat

leak-2.query: instances keep restarting hours after a release; callers see failures that leave no line, and the failures started long after the deploy

none-1.query: requests fail with AccessDenied when checkout-api writes orders, right after a permissions change; latency and pool wait are normal

none-2.query: checkout returns 200 but orders are saved twice; duplicate orders in the table, no errors and normal latency

none-3.query: one client is getting 400 responses for malformed request bodies; no other client is affected

none-4.query: GET /products is slow on its own while database query time, pool wait and payments-api are all flat

fresh-pool-1.query: all the shown errors are pool-acquisition timeouts and every route fails the same way; active connections are capped at the new limit while concurrency keeps rising

fresh-pool-2.query: pool wait went from near zero to hundreds of milliseconds in the minute of a config change; query time is normal and no request has failed yet, so this is latency from queueing, not errors

fresh-pool-3.query: concurrency climbed past what the connection pool can serve; requests that waited out the acquire timeout return 500, and the version on the failing lines is the one that ran fine before

fresh-deploy-1.query: new errors right after a redeploy; the failing requests return in a fraction of a millisecond and their lines carry no pool or payments fields

fresh-deploy-2.query: every successful checkout in the same window carries a promo, and every failing line has has_promo false with the same top frame in its stack

fresh-deploy-3.query: the error rate was zero in every minute before the deploy, then a steady share of requests fails with an exception the previous version never raised

fresh-downstream-1.query: checkout p99 tracks the payments latency and is over the threshold; there are no failed requests, so this is a latency problem only

fresh-downstream-2.query: the first payments timeouts in the window match the logged UpstreamTimeout lines, while the DB pool wait stays near zero and query time is normal

fresh-downstream-3.query: payments-api latency was normal before the incident and spiked to nearly the timeout in the alarm minute; product and cart routes are unaffected

fresh-leak-1.query: cold_start lines keep appearing although req is flat and concurrent_max stays well under the cap; nothing is logged as an error

fresh-leak-2.query: callers report failed checkouts that have no matching request line here, and the only release went out earlier in the day, well before the first failure

fresh-leak-3.query: requests disappear: callers count failures this service never logged, while pool wait, query time and payments-api stay flat and new instances keep starting
